subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or wait for the broader per-session tool-policy design to define cron tool boundaries?
rationale: This changes a hard tool-access boundary and public config shape, and cleanup automation cannot safely choose precedence against existing policy layers or the broader RFC.

options.title: Design cron policy inside the session-policy model
options.body: Use the broader per-session/tool-capability direction to define cron precedence first, then implement cron enforcement on that canonical path.

options.title: Add a dedicated cron scope now
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.*` as a narrow global cron policy and explicitly document that deny wins over per-job `toolsAllow` where needed.

options.title: Keep per-job toolsAllow only
options.body: Decline a global cron policy and document per-job allow-lists plus delivery safeguards as the supported operator workflow.

recommendation.title: Design cron policy inside the session-policy model
recommendation.body: Use the broader per-session/tool-capability direction to define cron precedence first, then implement cron enforcement on that canonical path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the prior reviewer on this issue and has recent history on cron/session capability paths.
